why: next@16.3.3+ and sharp@0.35.4 cleared the two next RCE advisories (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4) and the sharp/libheif advisory (GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c) — real patch-version bumps, not baselined. maplibre-gl's GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579 (DOM.sanitize() XSS in the attribution control, aka CVE-2026-85061) was previously baselined here because the installed 4.7.1 predated the vulnerable code (sanitize() was only added in 5.0.0, so 4.7.1 sat inside the advisory's stated '<= 6.4.0' range without containing the flaw). That baseline is gone as of 2026-09-23: maplibre-gl was bumped straight to 6.4.1, the actual fixed version, so the entry is removed rather than carried forward stale. 6.4.1 was chosen deliberately over any 5.0.0-6.4.0 version, since per the code-history analysis above those versions ARE genuinely vulnerable — re-verify this reasoning before ever downgrading maplibre-gl.
